checks.label: ADB Keys Present
checks.description: Presence of adb_keys may indicate previously trusted host
checks.remediation: Remove unauthorized keys with 'adb shell rm /data/misc/adb/adb_keys' and reboot the device.

checks.label: ADB Over Network Port
checks.description: service.adb.tcp.port should be empty/disabled. Any value means network ADB is configured. This check flags the configuration as a warning; the companion 'Network ADB Bound To Loopback Only' check escalates to critical only when the socket is actually exposed beyond loopback.
checks.remediation: Disable ADB over network by running 'adb shell setprop service.adb.tcp.port -1' and restarting ADB.

checks.label: System Debug Binaries
checks.description: Presence of debug tools increases attack surface
checks.remediation: Remove debug binaries with 'adb shell rm /system/bin/gdbserver /system/bin/strace' on a remounted system.

checks.label: Kernel DebugFS Enabled
checks.description: Kernel debugfs enabled exposes sensitive kernel interfaces
checks.remediation: Disable debugfs by setting CONFIG_DEBUG_FS=n in the kernel config and rebuilding the boot image.

checks.label: ADB Shell Running As Root (service.adb.root)
checks.description: service.adb.root=1 means adbd is running as root and 'adb shell' returns uid=0. On production user builds this must be 0 or unset. Combined with ro.debuggable=0 and ro.adb.secure=1 this enforces shell-user-only ADB access.
checks.remediation: Set service.adb.root=0. Use a user build (ro.build.type=user) so adbd drops privileges. Run 'adb unroot' to demote a running adbd.

checks.label: Network ADB Bound To Loopback Only
checks.command: P=$(getprop service.adb.tcp.port 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$P" ] || [ "$P" = "-1" ] || [ "$P" = "0" ]; then echo DISABLED; else ADDRS=$( (netstat -tln 2>/dev/null || ss -tln 2>/dev/null) | grep -E ":$P([^0-9]|$)" | awk '{print $4}'); NONLOOP=$(printf '%s\n' "$ADDRS" | grep -vE '^(127\.0\.0\.1|::1|\[::1\])[:.]'); if [ -n "$NONLOOP" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$NONLOOP" | head -3; else echo LOOPBACK_ONLY; fi; fi
checks.description: If network ADB is enabled (service.adb.tcp.port set), the adbd socket must bind to loopback only. A non-loopback bind (e.g. 0.0.0.0) exposes ADB to the LAN with no IP allowlist enforcement, which has been used in IoT and POS compromises. This check inspects every bind for the configured port (not just the first) so a dual-stack loopback+wildcard bind cannot mask the exposure.
checks.remediation: Disable network ADB ('setprop service.adb.tcp.port -1') or front it with an SSH tunnel. Android core does not provide a per-IP allowlist for adbd; gate access at the network layer (firewall, MAC filter, VLAN).

checks.label: USB Debugging User Notification (persist.adb.notify)
checks.description: persist.adb.notify controls the persistent 'USB debugging connected' status bar notification. A value of 0 hides the notification, which has been observed in malicious carrier customisations and tampered ROMs to keep ADB sessions invisible to the operator. Empty or 1 is safe.
checks.remediation: Set persist.adb.notify=1 or remove the override so Android shows the default debugging notification. Investigate any ROM that ships persist.adb.notify=0.

checks.label: adbd Binary Integrity (SHA-256 Baseline)
checks.command: if [ -x /system/bin/adbd ]; then sha256sum /system/bin/adbd 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}'; else echo 'MISSING'; fi
checks.description: Records the SHA-256 of /system/bin/adbd so the operator can diff it against a known-good per-build baseline. dm-verity should already catch tampering on locked devices; this check exposes drift on devices where verity is disabled or the system partition is remounted rw. MISSING means adbd is absent or not executable.
checks.remediation: Record this hash per firmware build. If the value changes between audits on the same build, treat as a system partition tamper indicator and reflash the stock system image. With --save-baseline / --baseline this comparison is automatic.
